page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4ms_v2 is a constrained-vCPU virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, tailored for workloads requiring an extreme memory footprint alongside high-frequency single-thread execution. The hardware profile is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Although based on a larger underlying chassis, this specific configuration exposes 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading (2 threads per core). It features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an expansive 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AMX (tile and int8), and hardware crypto acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

A defining aspect of this instance is its massive allocation of 336.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 84.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This ratio heavily diverges from standard compute configurations and provides enormous in-memory capacity. The server does not bundle local disk storage, requiring network-attached premium storage for persistent workloads, and includes no GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the high 4.2 GHz clock rate delivers strong single-core results, registering in the top 10% for Geekbench single-core performance (score: 2278.0) and top 25% for single-threaded compression tasks. However, total compute throughput is bounded by the 4-vCPU limit, leading to lower multi-threaded benchmark rankings, such as weak stress-ng multi-core metrics and Clang software compilation scores.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core count lowers per-core software licensing expenses—frequently a major cost driver for enterprise database software—while retaining the substantial 336.0 GB RAM allocation and top-tier single-core performance. This makes the Azure FX16-4ms_v2 well matched for memory-intensive, per-core licensed databases, in-memory caches, and specialized analytical applications requiring vast memory capacity without paying for unneeded vCPUs.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 260 MB of L3 cache, complemented by vector extensions like AVX-512 and AMX. The instance delivers an exceptional 336.0 GB of RAM (84.0 GB per vCPU), zero bundled local storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark metrics reveal top-tier single-core Geekbench performance (2278.0) and strong single-threaded compression speeds, though overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU count. The instance is an effective choice for memory-heavy enterprise databases, large Redis deployments, and analytical caching tasks bounded by software licensing costs.
